articles.title: USA Wins As Pulisic's Epic Bicycle Kick Goal Sends Pochettino Out On High Note
articles.summary: Christian Pulisic scored on a sensational bicycle kick as the United States sent coach Mauricio Pochettino out on a successful note.
articles.body: Christian Pulisic scored on a sensational bicycle kick as the United States sent coach Mauricio Pochettino out on a successful note, defeating Haiti 2-0 on Tuesday night in the second leg of the Nations League quarterfinals. Pochettino received warm applause from the crowd of 24,001 at TQL Stadium after two years leading the Americans. The 54-year-old Argentine begins his new job as Manchester United's coach on Wednesday after agreeing last Friday to replace Michael Carrick. Goalkeeper coach Toni Jiménez, top assistant Jesús Pérez and fitness coach Sebastiano Pochettino — Mauricio Pochettino's son — have been in England since Sunday. They departed after the U.S. defeated Haiti 6-0 on Saturday in the first leg. Assistant coach Miguel D’Agostino, fitness coach Sylvia Tuyà Viñas and analyst Alex Scott stayed for Tuesday's match and are also headed to Manchester with Pochettino. Pochettino had a 23-12-2 record with the U.S., including a run to the round of 16 at this year’s World Cup before a 4-1 loss to Belgium. He used the same starting 11 from Saturday's match. During Pochettino's tenure, 78 players earned caps, including 31 who made their national team debuts. Nine teenagers also earned playing time, including the 18-year-old Julian Hall, who scored in the 43rd minute Tuesday. The Americans won the series by an aggregate score of 8-0 to advance to the four-match knockout CONCACAF Nations League Finals in March in Los Angeles. Pulisic had three goals in the matches against Haiti. He lined up and directed a bicycle kick off the far post in the 25th minute after McKennie lobbed a crossing pass. Pulisic, who has 36 goals for the U.S., was subbed out in the 65th minute. Hall, who scored for the fifth time in six U.S. appearances, controlled a pass from McKennie before directing it past Haiti goalkeeper Alexandre Pierre. Pochettino will have a couple of days to work with his new squad before United visits Liverpool on Sunday. Pochettino — who previously coached in the Premier League at Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea — is United’s eighth permanent coach or manager since Alex Ferguson retired in 2013. Next Steps In New U.S. Coach Search U.S. Soccer CEO JT Batson said in a prematch interview with TNT Sports that Pochettino has shown everyone the benefits of coming to America as well as his confidence in being able to attract a world-class coach. Pochettino said during a roundtable with reporters on Monday that Pep Guardiola should be his successor if offered the job. Guardiola won 12 domestic trophies and two UEFA Champions League titles at Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City. "For us to win, we need to be great at a lot of things, and we need someone who cares about youth development, cares about our youth national team programs, our relationships with our clubs and the success of the federation more broadly," Batson said. "We know that is a key part of our success, and it’s also a key part of how we’ve been able to attract great people because they get to do big things." Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Klatt’s CFP Takeaways: Alabama At No. 3 Is ‘Absurd,’ Big Ten Teams Are Lurking
articles.summary: Joel Klatt thinks the College Football Playoff committee took a wrong turn with Alabama at No. 3, and he sees a Big 12 with a legitimate chance at multiple bids and a trio of Big Ten teams lurking.
articles.body: Joel Klatt thinks the College Football Playoff committee took a wrong turn with Alabama at No. 3, and he sees a Big 12 with a legitimate chance at multiple bids and a trio of Big Ten teams lurking. The committee left its top four unchanged in its third rankings Tuesday night, with Georgia at No. 1, followed by Utah, two-loss Alabama and undefeated UCLA. Texas moved up to No. 5 after winning at LSU, two spots behind the Crimson Tide. Alabama held its spot even though its three best wins, over LSU, South Carolina and Kentucky, all lost last weekend. On the latest episode of "The Joel Klatt Show," Klatt called Alabama’s ranking "absurd," accused the committee of building an "echo chamber" around the SEC and said it didn’t apply the logic it used on Indiana a week earlier. Here are Joel Klatt’s takeaways: 1.Why Is Alabama No. 3? Klatt’s thoughts: "Obviously, Alabama at three is absurd. I tell you, the team I actually feel worst for is Texas, and they’re in the SEC, and they’re getting absolutely hosed by the committee. Does anyone in the committee actually have the schedules in front of them? Texas has wins over Tennessee and Ohio State. Bama doesn’t have anything close to that. "Nine teams ranked. Well, because the SEC, the feedback loop. Obviously, the SEC is so tough. Got it. Why is the SEC so tough? Well, because Alabama is number three. Do you see the feedback loop? Do you see the echo chamber that we’re building? We’ve got the driver that took the wrong turn, doesn’t want to admit that they went in the wrong direction, so they’re just driving aimlessly right now through the woods. … We’ve got South Carolina losing by 28 to 3-6 Arkansas, and they’re 21st in the country. Why? To prop up Alabama?" 2.Big 12 Has A Clear Path Utah is No. 2 after its 40-39 win at Arizona, a game Klatt called on FOX. BYU is No. 10 and Texas Tech is No. 12. Klatt’s thoughts: "I think there is a legitimate chance, obviously, for two [Big 12 teams], because if things hold where they’re at, you’re going to get two teams in with BYU and then the champ. In this case, it would be Utah. But by the way, there’s still hope for a third, because Texas Tech could actually win the conference championship. They’ve got a clean path towards the conference championship, and if they were to win, let’s say over Utah, Utah would stay in, and then Tech would be in there, and then maybe BYU is still in there." 3.Big Ten Teams Are Lurking UCLA is No. 4 and Indiana is No. 8, with Oregon, Ohio State and Iowa just outside the field at Nos. 13, 14 and 15. Klatt’s thoughts: "And then you’ve got that trio of Big Ten teams, and that’s the last thing that I would say on this: Oregon is sitting there, just kind of lurking at 13. "Remember, Indiana got dropped five spots last week during a bye week. Last week, all five of Indiana’s best wins lost, and that was the rationale that was given to us by the committee. This week, all five of Alabama’s best wins lost. The same exact logic that was applied last week wasn’t applied this week, so they’re not consistent. They’re stubborn. I feel like we’re in an Orwell novel right now. They’re asking us to suspend all of our faculties and just believe what they give us, and I refuse to do that." FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. articles.title: Who Are FIFA's Presidential Election Candidates To Replace Gianni Infantino?
articles.summary: Here are the candidates to potentially replace FIFA president Gianni Infantino and pertinent details regarding the election process.
articles.body: No sitting FIFA president has lost a re-election contest since 1974. Gianni Infantino has the weight of history on his side trying to extend his 11-year presidency of soccer’s governing body to 2031, with a deadline of midnight Wednesday in Zurich (2300GMT) for challengers to enter the race. Infantino was expected to run unopposed until a global backlash sparked in July by media reports of his secretive plan to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors. The March 18 vote is now turning into a three-way contest between Infantino and challengers from France and Japan. Who Are The Candidates? Gianni Infantino: The 56-year-old Swiss-Italian lawyer became FIFA’s president in 2016, replacing Sepp Blatter who resigned after a corruption scandal. Under his leadership, FIFA expanded the men’s World Cup from 32 to 48 teams, brought VAR video reviews to the tournament and increased development funding for member federations. He was cruising toward re-election for a third straight time until his now scrapped FIFA Forward Enterprise Plan prompted dozens of national federations, mostly in Europe, to withdraw their support. Kohzo Tashima: Turns 69 on Saturday, a former Japan international player who later coached youth national teams. At the Japan soccer federation, he has been general secretary, president, and now honorary president. Since 2015, Asian federations elected him as one of their representatives on FIFA’s ruling committee. Philippe Diallo: The 63-year-old president of the French Football Federation since 2023. A veteran sports administrator though recent arrival into international soccer politics. Elected in April 2023 to the executive committee of European soccer body UEFA. Until this crisis, was seen as loyal to Infantino. Ramon Vega: A 55-year-old former Switzerland and Tottenham player who has said he wants to be a candidate for the fourth straight FIFA election. Vega didn’t have the necessary endorsements to get on the ballot in his previous attempts, and it’s unclear whether he does this time. What's At Stake? At the core of the election is how FIFA governs the world of soccer at a time when commercial interests play an ever-growing role in the game. Infantino has been an increasingly executive boss pushing to create new, bigger and more lucrative FIFA competitions for national and club teams with little if any consultation. World Cups got bigger, more profitable – directing ever more money to FIFA voters – but a drive to play every two years instead of four failed. Continental bodies like UEFA have seen Infantino’s expansionism as a threat to their events, like the Champions League and European Championship. Soccer leaders in Asia, Europe and the North Americas were blindsided and furious by the FFE plan, which they called trust-breaking deception by Infantino. Under the plan, investors led by Joshua Kushner – the brother of President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner – would pay $4.2 billion for a 20%-plus stake in FFE. That would fund $20 million payments to each of the 211 members who effectively own FIFA. The plan also reignited unease at Infantino breaching FIFA’s statutory political neutrality by unilaterally aligning with Trump: giving him FIFA’s Peace Prize, leasing an office in Trump Tower in Manhattan and not enforcing a mandatory red-card ban for U.S. forward Folarin Balogun in an unprecedented World Cup controversy. Infantino, who has apologized for how the FFE plan was presented, still has widespread support among federations outside Europe, including Latin America and Africa, who have benefited from more development money from FIFA. He has promised to use FIFA reserves to significantly increase the money national federations receive to $25 million between 2027-2030. How Does the Election Process Work? Candidates for the FIFA presidency had to apply by midnight in Zurich (2300 GMT) on Wednesday with written support from at least five of the 211 member federations. They must also have had an "active role" in soccer – "as a player or an official within FIFA, a confederation or an association," the FIFA Governance Regulations state – for two of the past five years. Candidacies are put to a FIFA-appointed three-person election panel: Swiss accountant Bruno Chiomento, governance expert Chris Mihm of the U.S. and Jamaican sports official Molly Rhone. The panel has until Feb. 18 to confirm which candidates passed eligibility and integrity checks to advance to a secret ballot on March 18 in Rabat, Morocco. The panel’s rulings can be appealed against at the Court of Arbitration for Sport in Lausanne, Switzerland. The FIFA timetable could run alongside against expected attempts by newly empowered Democrats in the U.S. Congress to summon Infantino to a hearing. Meanwhile, UEFA has asked U.S. courts to authorize evidence discovery for a possible criminal complaint against Infantino in Switzerland. FIFA has accused UEFA of a "smear campaign. How Many Votes Are Needed To Win? Infantino needs support from 106 of the 211 members to win re-election. An AP tally shows he currently has 105, based on announcements by member federations in recent months. More than 50 federations have not announced a position. While 50 nations have declared opposition to Infantino, only a handful of have publicly endorsed one of the challengers, though that is likely to change in coming weeks. In a three-candidate election, votes from two-thirds of the eligible members are needed to win in the first round. In the second round, the candidate with the fewest votes is eliminated, and then a simple majority will win. It is set to be just the third time in the past 50 years that an incumbent FIFA president had an opponent on the ballot paper. In 2002 and 2015, Sepp Blatter won handily each time against a single opponent amid allegations of mismanagement fueling fury from much of Europe aimed at the Swiss head of FIFA whose reputation was hit hard. What Is The FIFA President's Job? The statutory requirement is to "foster a positive image of FIFA," protect its strategic direction and policies "as defined" by the 37-member ruling Council the president chairs. He also must chair its annual Congress, though not always on time. The FIFA president also must "maintain and develop good relations" with continental bodies, member federations, "political bodies and international organizations." Those duties included working with leaders of World Cup host nations, which in Infantino’s presidency has meant Vladimir Putin in Russia, Trump in the U.S. and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Saudi Arabia. Infantino has effusively praised both those men and, much more than Blatter, has attended — and clearly relished — events like G20 meetings, the World Economic Forum at Davos, and economic conferences backed by Saudi Arabia, the men’s 2034 World Cup host. "It’s like a monarchy," said Alex Phillips, a longtime former colleague of Infantino at UEFA and FIFA, said Tuesday at a soccer conference in Brussels, "where you try and get as close to the king as possible to get influence for your decision." Infantino earned close to $6 million last year at current exchange rates, plus housing expenses and use of a private jet tied to Qatar Airways’ sponsorship of the World Cup. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: The Rock Reveals Status for WWE Survivor Series 2026 in Video Amid 30th Anniversary of Debut
articles.summary: WWE legend Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson revealed Wednesday that he will be in attendance for Survivor Series in Houston on Nov. 28.
articles.body:
WWE legend Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson revealed Wednesday that he will be in attendance for Survivor Series in Houston on Nov. 28.

The Rock broke the news during an appearance on the Pat McAfee Show , saying, "I would not miss next week for the world, man. So, I'm going to Houston. Houston, we don't have a problem. I'm going to Houston and I'm gonna go to Survivor Series."

Predicting Final Members of Team USA and Team Mexico 🔮

Fittingly, Survivor Series 2026 marks the 30-year anniversary of The Rock's WWE debut, as he competed in a four-on-four elimination match at Survivor Series 1996 under the name Rocky Maivia.

While the Rocky Maivia character was ultimately rejected by the fans, The Rock went on to become one of the biggest stars in pro wrestling history, and it all started at Survivor Series.

Even before The Rock made his announcement regarding Survivor Series on Wednesday, WWE had been celebrating the 30th anniversary of his debut in myriad ways, including the creation of a limited-edition Rocky Maivia Intercontinental Championship belt, which was made available for purchase on WWE Shop .

Although The Rock is part of the TKO board of directors, he is often busy with his hugely successful acting career, so his WWE appearances tend to be few and far between.

However, The Great One told McAfee on Wednesday that he made a special request to push back the press tour for his upcoming Jumanji: Open World in order to make it possible for him to attend Survivor Series.

It is unclear if there are plans for The Rock to be featured on the show in any way, but given his star power, there is little doubt that WWE would love to give him a segment at Survivor Series.

The Rock being present for the premium live event may also fuel speculation regarding him potentially getting involved in the likely main event pitting The Bloodline against 946 in a WarGames match.

Since The Bloodline is made up entirely of The Rock's family members in Roman Reigns, The Usos, Solo Sikoa and Jacob Fatu, perhaps he could lend a helping hand.

Even if that doesn't come to fruition, simply having The Rock on hand for the 30th anniversary of his iconic career is a massive deal for WWE in its own right.

articles.title: Salva Ballesta, más conciliador que nunca ante las elecciones generales: "Que gane España"
articles.standfirst: El exfutbolista reivindica la figura de Luis de la Fuente, destaca su credibilidad y capacidad para tomar decisiones y apuesta por dejar a un lado las diferencias políticas para trabajar por el bien del país
articles.summary: El exfutbolista reivindica la figura de Luis de la Fuente, destaca su credibilidad y capacidad para tomar decisiones y apuesta por dejar a un lado las diferencias políticas para trabajar por el bien del país
articles.body: Salva Ballesta ha mostrado su perfil más conciliador en su entrevista en el Programa de Ortega, donde ha abordado diferentes cuestiones de actualidad deportiva y política. Con las elecciones generales en el horizonte, el exfutbolista ha lanzado un mensaje de unidad por encima de las siglas y las diferencias ideológicas: "Que gane España". Una declaración con la que ha defendido la necesidad de remar todos en la misma dirección para que el país siga creciendo y aprovechando sus fortalezas. En clave futbolística, Ballesta también ha tenido tiempo para hablar del derbi sevillano, una de las citas que despierta mayor pasión en el fútbol español, y de nombres propios como Julián Alvarez, protagonista del panorama futbolístico por su rendimiento y su capacidad para marcar diferencias. El exdelantero ha compartido sus reflexiones sobre la actualidad del deporte rey, sin perder de vista el papel de los grandes protagonistas del fútbol nacional e internacional. Uno de los momentos más destacados de la conversación ha llegado al hablar de Luis de la Fuente, al que Ballesta ha dedicado numerosos elogios. El exfutbolista ha definido al seleccionador español como "un tío extraordinario", tanto por su calidad humana como por su trayectoria deportiva. Además, ha destacado su conocimiento de los jugadores desde las categorías inferiores y su capacidad para tomar decisiones sin dejarse llevar por las presiones externas. Preguntado incluso por la posibilidad de que De la Fuente llegase a ser presidente del Gobierno, ha puesto el acento en una cualidad fundamental: "Tiene algo muy importante que tiene que tener una persona que desarrolla un cargo público, que es credibilidad". En el terreno político, Ballesta ha evitado posicionarse a favor de unas siglas concretas y ha defendido la importancia de acudir a las urnas y participar en las elecciones. "Hay que ir a votar y ya está", ha señalado, antes de insistir en que lo verdaderamente importante es el futuro colectivo. El exdelantero ha reivindicado las virtudes del país, desde su gastronomía y su situación geográfica hasta su gente, su cultura y sus éxitos deportivos. "Estamos en lo alto de la ola", ha apuntado, convencido de que España tiene potencial de sobra para aspirar a ser uno de los mejores países del mundo.

articles.title: WWE Rumors on Bronson Reed Surgery, Undertaker Talks Final In-Ring Action, Sheamus Fuels AEW Buzz
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Latest on Reed After Crown Jewel Injury, Surgery

Predicting Final Members of Team USA and Team Mexico 🔮

Bronson Reed is reportedly back in the United States after suffering a scary injury at Crown Jewel in Saudi Arabia on Nov. 7.

According to Bryan Alvarez of Wrestling Observer Live (h/t WrestlePurists ), Reed underwent surgery and he is currently recovering at home after initially being unable to fly back to the U.S. with the rest of the WWE roster and crew in Saudi Arabia.

Reed did not have a match at Crown Jewel, but he interfered during the World Tag Team Championship match that saw The Vision's Bron Breakker and Austin Theory put the titles on the line against Penta and Je'Von Evans.

While Reed gave The Vision the numbers advantage, Oba Femi quickly changed that by showing up and wrecking shop.

Femi even threw Reed off the stage and through some tables, which appeared to be the moment when Reed got injured.

Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp was the first to report that Reed had to stay back in Saudi Arabia with a "top international executive and a member of [WWE's] medical team" due to the injury.

Alvarez (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News) later reported that Reed had suffered multiple broken ribs and a lacerated kidney on the spot with Femi.

Although the latest Reed update is a positive one, it remains unclear when he could potentially return to in-ring action.

For now, the injury-plagued Vision is down an important member once again, leaving Breakker and Theory to continue carrying the load from an in-ring perspective.

WWE Hall of Famer The Undertaker suggested this week that his days of in-ring physicality may be over.

On Wednesday's episode of the Six Feet Under podcast (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News), The Undertaker interviewed Trick Williams, and the discussion turned to an in-ring segment they had on NXT in July 2025:

Williams brought up that he was the last person The Undertaker chokeslammed, prompting Taker to make a somewhat stunning declaration.

The Deadman said, "And I'm pretty sure, like, I'm almost 100 [percent] that you'll be the last too," before adding that he doesn't "foresee" himself ever executing another chokeslam.

While the 61-year-old Undertaker has been retired from in-ring competition since having his last match against AJ Styles at WrestleMania 36 in 2020, that hasn't stopped him from dishing out some punishment here and there since then.

Most notably, The Undertaker was one of many Superstars to run in during the main event of WrestleMania 40 between Roman Reigns and Cody Rhodes, taking out The Rock with a chokeslam.

As of now, Williams is the last chokeslam on his résumé, as The Phenom laid out the then-TNA world champion more than a year ago.

Taker didn't completely close the door on chokeslamming someone else in the future, but it does sound like he has largely moved on from that aspect of his career.

The Undertaker is currently a key creative force in WWE's version of AAA in Mexico, and that seems to be keeping him busy to the point that in-ring physicality is no longer a top priority.

Sheamus Shares Photo with AEW Star Amid Free Agency

Former WWE star Sheamus got fans talking this week when he posted a photo alongside a current AEW star.

In a post Tuesday on X, Sheamus shared multiple photos alongside Kazuchika Okada, who is the reigning AEW international champion:

Both Sheamus and Okada were in attendance for the world premiere event for the upcoming movie The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping .

While it doesn't necessarily mean Sheamus is AEW-bound, posing for pictures with a prominent AEW wrestler is a surefire way to generate speculation.

The 48-year-old Sheamus has not wrestled a match since November 2025 when he competed in his final WWE bout, teaming with John Cena and Rey Mysterio to beat The Judgment Day's Dominik Mysterio, JD McDonagh and Finn Balor.

Fightful Select (h/t Geno Mrosko of Cageside Seats) reported in July that Sheamus would be departing WWE at the conclusion of his contract after rejecting an offer to rework his deal.

It was later reported by Fightful Select (h/t Fightful's Ishaan Sharma ) that Sheamus officially became a free agent on Oct. 1.

That means The Celtic Warrior has been free and clear to sign elsewhere for well over a month, but every indication is that he has yet to do so.

If Sheamus does decide to continue wrestling outside of WWE, AEW would be a natural landing spot.

In addition to being the second-biggest wrestling company, AEW has never been shy about signing former WWE stars.

Just a few months ago, AEW signed Kofi and Austin Creed on the heels of their lengthy WWE runs, and Sheamus is in a similar category, as he had been with WWE since 2007.

Should Sheamus be the next WWE veteran to make the leap to AEW, it is easy to envision him having a match and potentially even a lengthy rivalry with Okada for the international title.

articles.title: GTA 6 release: Here's how the sports world will be affected by the most anticipated video game of all time
articles.summary: One NBA veteran predicted every sports league would see performance declines once GTA 6 releases.
articles.body:
After more than a decade of waiting, Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here. You probably heard a little something about it.

The game, which has already received near-perfect reviews , is set to upend the world Thursday … and potentially beyond. With estimates that roughly 16 million copies of the game were preordered, employers could be dealing with a lot of "sick" days ahead of the weekend.

That might sound farfetched, but it's true. Experts are estimating businesses in the United States could lose over $1 billion in productivity due to worker absences .

Given the anticipation for the game, and the popularity of gaming as a hobby in general, it should come as no surprise the sports world is going to be affected by the release of GTA 6.

The Miami Heat might be the most obvious example of that phenomenon, as the team will wear "Vice City" jerseys and play on a "Vice City" court when they take on the Milwaukee Bucks on Wednesday.

The team will also rebrand concession stands to match those in the game and play music from the game's soundtrack, per The Athletic.

Vice City is the fictionalized city in which GTA takes place. It's modeled after Miami. It's not the first time Vice City has appeared in the franchise. It was also the setting of Grand Theft Auto: Vice City, which was released in 2002.

The impact of GTA 6 on the sporting world is expected to go even deeper than that, though.

In September, Houston Rockets big man Steven Adams went so far as to say every major sporting league will see league-wide performance decline once the game releases in November.

Adams didn't just include the players when discussing the issue. He said coaches and scouts will also struggle to focus, thanks to GTA 6.

There's at least some precedent for that phenomenon. Back when Grand Theft Auto V was released in 2013, former Ottawa Senators goalie Craig Anderson said his performance suffered due to the game's release, per the Hockey News.

"My worst season that I felt I had in Ottawa, was the year that 'Grand Theft Auto V' came out," Anderson said. "Direct correlation. Just a time suck. You'd play after a game, you'd get home 11-11:30, you'd start playing that game and it'd be 4 AM and you'd be like 'I'm not even tired.'"

As the GTA 6 release date inched closer, other athletes seemingly confirmed Adams' prediction. Los Angeles Rams wideout Tutu Atwell said he already told his mom she "might not hear from me for a couple of days" due to the game's release, per the New York Post. Atwell, who is a lifelong fan of the series, added that he's been "waiting for this one for a long, long time." It's been 13 years since the last iteration of the video game series.

His approach is going to be a common one among athletes. Heat sharpshooter Klay Thompson essentially said the exact same thing when asked about GTA 6.

"I am an avid gamer. I've been playing GTA since it was the bird's eye view on the original Playstation. I'm 36, but I'll still be gaming when I get this version, and the story mode of this game is maybe the best in all of gaming."

Thompson added, "It will feel much better to have a day of gaming when we get that victory [over the Bucks] on Wednesday."

The Cleveland Browns — whose players must be incredibly grateful to be on a bye on the week of the game's release — have spent a fair amount of time this week thinking about GTA, per quarterback Deshaun Watson.

While some of those quotes might be worrisome to fans of those teams, most athletes seem to understand the importance of their day jobs.

Rams guard Steve Avila and New York Jets running back Breece Hall were among those who acknowledge the game will affect athletes, but not in a worrisome way, per the New York Post.

"I think a lot of athletes are responsible," Avila said. "But if you could check guys' sleep scores … I think you'd see that some guys' hours are going to go way down, for sure."

Hall said he would make sure he gets his film work in early so he can give himself an extra hour or so with the game later in the day. He added, "You've got to make sure you handle the main thing first before you have some fun."

In addition to not wanting to perform worse on the field, athletes know their every move is under a microscope these days, even when it comes to gaming. Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray was forced to face some uncomfortable questions back in 2022 after a fan on Reddit broke down how much worse Murray performs in NFL games when Call of Duty holds Double XP weekends.

Murray took those theories in stride, eventually partnering with Activision , the company that makes games in the Call of Duty franchise, in 2024.

Any chance of a Murray-like conspiracy would take weeks to uncover. And even then, given the nature of small-sample sizes in sports, equating a slumping player's performance with playing too much GTA 6 will be too hard to definitively prove.

Like everyone else, athletes will be eagerly playing GTA 6 in the weeks after its release. And, also like everyone else, that might lead to some more fatigued days at the office, even when they are trying to be responsible gamers.

articles.title: UConn's $32 million-plus Gampel Pavilion naming deal lands in court over a promise made in 1989
articles.summary: Harry A. Gampel's daughters allege UConn's $32.5 million M&T Bank deal broke a 1989 promise that his name would grace Gampel Pavilion in perpetuity.
articles.body: In 1989, Harry A. Gampel gave UConn $1 million to help build a basketball arena. The university’s president promised in writing that the building would bear Gampel’s name "in perpetuity." Thirty-seven years later, three of Gampel’s daughters are suing over a 20-year naming deal with M&T Bank that CT Insider reported is worth $32.5 million. Margo Gampel Absher, Debra Gampel Fischman and Linda Gampel Abrahamson filed suit Nov. 11 in Hartford Superior Court against UConn’s Board of Trustees and the state of Connecticut. The sisters allege the deal violates the terms of their father’s gift by giving the bank’s name more prominence on the building. They are asking a judge to order UConn to restore prominent exterior signage bearing the full name, Harry A. Gampel Pavilion. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Richard Weinstein, the family’s attorney, told OutKick in an email that his clients "are not looking for money." He said the family wants the arena called Harry A. Gampel Pavilion at M&T Bank Center, with both names displayed in lettering of the same size. Weinstein said he presented that exact proposal to UConn but received no response. In a statement to OutKick, UConn said it "continues to honor and revere Harry A. articles.title: Luke Littler stunned by Jermaine Wattimena in last 16 at Grand Slam of Darts as title defence ends
articles.summary: Luke Littler was beaten 10-8 by Jermaine Wattimena in the last 16 at the Grand Slam of Darts; It brings his title defence to an end; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports until November 22
articles.body:
It was simply a stunning performance from Wattimena in which he averaged 101.7, outscoring the world No 1 and outplaying him in every facet, hitting 10 180s and 11 140s on the way.

The loss for Littler means he will not join Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen on a short but illustrious list of players who have won the Grand Slam three times in a row.

Littler had picked up the Grand Slam title in 2024 with a win over Martin Lukeman and then backed that up with victory over Luke Humphries in 2025. But his attempt at a hat-trick was shattered with Wattimena's win blowing the competition wide open.

"It feels emotional, absolutely incredible," Wattimena told Sky Sports immediately after the victory.

"I saved my best game for this stage and I'm really proud of it.

"I was 7-2 ahead and missed three darts to go 8-2 up. He then started playing well again.

"But in the last leg, one dart for the match - it feels amazing."

Wattimena will now face Kevin Doets after he came through with a classy 10-5 victory over Cameron Menzies.

The match was close and went with the throw until the 10th leg when Doets landed D16 for a two-leg advantage. From there, he claimed three legs on the spin before Menzies got another on the board and then took the match with his 10th 180 and then match dart at D4.

It was evident from early in the first session that Wattimena was going to give Littler a real game as he broke 'The Nuke's' throw twice to lead 3-2 going into the first break.

It was the second session in which he then found a level that even Littler could not match. Wattimena made it five legs in a row, secured two more breaks of throw, and was averaging as high as 107 before Littler stopped the rot and broke back to bring the score to 7-3.

The question for the Dutchman then was whether he could keep such an incredible level up. He was still scoring well, but Littler's level raised. When the reigning Grand Slam champion picked up three legs in a row to bring the score to 9-8, it looked as though he was going to pull off an almighty comeback.

But Wattimena closed the door on it. In the 18th leg, Wattimena had the darts for the match on 77 and took it out with a match dart on tops.

He then let out the emotions and tears of joy as he took in just what he had achieved.

Jermaine Wattimena is a Dutch darts player who has peaked as high as world No 16 in 2026 and won three titles in the last two years.

In fact, he beat Littler en route to his Players Championship title back in August.

This is his 11th year on the ProTour but the last two years have seen him reach new heights as he has slightly slowed his very fast throw down. He has reached the last 32 at the Worlds and the Masters and made the last 16 of the World Matchplay in 2025.

Sky Sports' John Part on Littler's loss…

"I said at the top of the show that Luke could be vulnerable if he didn't have the full respect of what could happen to him from his opponent.

"If you keep letting the same things happen, and let someone get ahead of you like that, you're not always going to catch them.

"Tonight was definitely Jermaine's night. He played superbly. He was the guy in top mode and not Luke."

Gerwyn Price came out on top in a high-class contest with Ryan Searle and made it into the quarter-finals of the Grand Slam with a 10-7 victory to continue his quest for a fourth Grand Slam title.

Price romped into a 4-1 lead in the first session, two breaks of throw and then a brilliant 148 finish bringing out the roar from the 'Iceman'.

But Searle came out in the second session and was scoring with ease, allowing him to take three of the five legs on offer but Price was still finding stunning moments, a 147 checkout then a 90 finish via T17 and tops moving him 6-4 ahead.

In the final session it was a real grudge match but Price's magnificent finishing kept him ahead despite Searle matching every break of throw.

A match dart came and went for Price and Searle took advantage to bring the game to 9-7 ahead. It did not take long though for Price's reply, as, in the 17th leg, Price landed his fourth attempt at a match dart in D10.

Next up, he will take on Niko Springer who is through to his first-ever TV quarter-final after a tough 10-8 victory over Rob Cross.

There was nothing separating the two until Springer went on a blistering burst that saw him race from 5-4 down to one leg from the quarters at 9-5 up.

That was when the nerves started to creep in, the trebling fell away, and Cross looked like he was coming back. 'Voltage' rattled off three legs in a row and was the man with the momentum.

However, Springer found the big darts at the key moment to take out 111 on tops and seal his spot in the last eight.

articles.title: Grand Slam of Darts 2026: Luke Littler shocked by Jermaine Wattimena in round two
articles.summary: Defending champion Luke Littler suffers a shock early exit at the Grand Slam of Darts after a stunning display from Jermaine Wattimena.
articles.body:
Defending champion Luke Littler suffered a shock early exit at the Grand Slam of Darts after a stunning display from Jermaine Wattimena.

The Dutchman was in tears after securing a remarkable, and thoroughly deserved, 10-8 victory in the second round in Wolverhampton.

Having looked imperious as he won six legs on the spin to take a 7-2 lead, 16th seed Wattimena showed signs of nerves as the finish line approached, but dug in to stave off a late Littler comeback and progress to the quarter-finals.

"I think I played really incredible, I played my best game on this stage and I'm really proud of it," an emotional Wattimena told Sky Sports.

"He started playing well at the end. Last leg, [I had] one dart for the match - amazing."

Wattimena finished with an average of 101.70 having hit a staggering 10 180s and, such was his level for the majority of the match, he might feel the margin of victory should have been more comfortable.

The 38-year-old twice threatened nine-darters and had two darts for an 8-2 lead, with Littler rarely even given a look at a double.

However, the 19-year-old world champion sensed an opportunity and showed his class with a 10-darter to break throw as Wattimena finally stuttered a leg from victory.

But a dramatic comeback fell just short as, with Littler waiting to pounce on 65, Wattimena hit tops to take out 77 for the match and reach the last eight of the tournament for a second time.

Wattimena will face compatriot Kevin Doets in the next round after the world number 23 saw off Scotland's Cameron Menzies 10-5.

Doets averaged 101.51 and matched Wattimena's 10 maximums as his relentless scoring made up for an off night on the doubles.

Fourth seed Gerwyn Price is also through after a clinical display to beat Englishman Ryan Searle 10-7.

The Welshman averaged 103.31 and hit 45% of his doubles to see off 13th seed Searle, who himself averaged just under 100.

Price will face Niko Springer for a place in the semi-finals after he overcame former world champion Rob Cross 10-8.

Cross averaged 96.05 to Springer's 88.59, but the German's finishing was far superior - with a checkout rate of 48% - and that proved the difference.

articles.title: Jermaine Wattimena wins Wolverhampton hearts with victory over Luke Littler: 'You beat him, the crowd loves you'
articles.summary: Jermaine Wattimena put in a stunning performance to come up with a 10-8 win and dump Luke Littler out of the Grand Slam in the second round; you can watch the Grand Slam of Darts in Wolverhampton live on Sky Sports until November 22
articles.body:
An English crowd chanting so heartily for a Dutch player is somewhat of a rarity, especially when they are taking on an Englishman, but it was the sensational manner of his victory over the world No 1 and back-to-back Grand Slam champion that won them over.

Littler was aiming for a Grand Slam three-peat after his wins in 2024 and 2025 but with the Dutchman prevailing, it is still only Phil Taylor and Michael van Gerwen who have achieved such a feat.

Wattimena led 3-2 before running away to get 7-2 up against Littler. He then held on as Littler fought back to 9-8 and pinned 77 on tops for what is now the biggest win of his career.

It was made all the sweeter given the fact Wattimena has felt the pain of a massive Littler comeback before. He was 7-2 up against 'The Nuke' at the Matchplay in 2025 before eventually being beaten.

"Brilliant. One word needed, brilliant," Wattimena said.

"To be honest, I was thinking about the Matchplay in 2025 when I was 7-2 up. Now I am feeling that again but then the 77 goes in.

"I beat Luke Humphries in the European Championship and this is a bigger win than Luke Humphries then.

"I think you have seen me playing and I played with a lot of confidence. I was really concentrating in the match and I think I can go further than this.

"To be honest, I always play well against Luke Littler but to finally beat him on stage, I am really happy with that.

"I think my scoring power was better than his scoring power. He had to do it against me as well, but I don't think he did.

"They sang my name and I was emotional. That was really brilliant.

"If you beat Luke Littler then the crowd loves you."

Wattimena beat Littler back in August on the way to picking up a Players Championship title.

It was that win that reinforced for Wattimena that he could do the same again on the TV stage.

"I think (that win) gave me some confidence and then you know that he is not unbeatable as well. He is a human, he is not a robot," he added.

"He is a good player, he's an amazing player, everyone knows it but I am more than happy to beat him here at the Grand Slam.

"He got me here two years ago with a high score, but now I got one back.

"When you go to a tournament, you have to think that you can win the title, to be honest.

"You play tournaments to win something. It is a long way to go, but I am here for a win.

"I have got a day off tomorrow, so I have got nothing to do. I will be jumping in the jacuzzi, jumping in the swimming pool, so I'm all relaxed tomorrow."

articles.title: Michael van Gerwen targets 'A-game' for James Wade meeting in last-16 clash of Grand Slam of Darts
articles.summary: Michael van Gerwen on his second-round opponent: "James Wade is playing some fantastic darts; he's probably in some of the best form of his life"; pair's meeting a rematch of 2016 final which MVG won; watch the Grand Slam of Darts on Sky Sports Main Event at 7pm, Thursday
articles.body:
Their clash on Thursday night - live on Sky Sports+ and Main Event from 7pm - is a rematch of the 2016 final, in which Van Gerwen claimed the second of his three consecutive titles.

But it's Wade, a three-time runner-up at the event, who is the form player of the pair leading into the last 16 matchup, having dropped only one leg across his two group-stage wins.

Van Gerwen, contrastingly, saw both his wins over Henry Coates and Jeffrey de Graaf come down to last-leg deciders. He averaged 100 against Coates, but that dropped to 90 against De Graaf, a match in which he missed seven match darts.

"It wasn't a good game at all," Van Gerwen, seeded 10th at the tournament, told Sky Sports after his victory over De Graaf.

"Sometimes you're not doing what you want to do. That's frustrating, because I know I'm capable of doing a lot more.

"What can I say? I am through to the next round - that's all history now - and it's onto the next one."

The former world No 1 added: "James Wade is playing some fantastic darts, you can't deny that. He's probably in some of the best form of his life.

"I need to make sure I play my A-game if I'm going to beat him - simple as that."

Wade has been in sensational form across 2026, making it to the final of the UK Open, winning the Australian Masters, Flanders Darts Trophy, and the opening Players Championship event back in February.

He knows that, with his form at the minute, he has the game to beat anyone, especially if the contest is a bit of a grudge match.

"I think I am way better than the top 10 but I have had to bumble along," said the seventh seed, who has averaged over 100 in both of his Grand Slam group stage wins against Cam Crabtree (5-1) and Ricky Evans (5-0).

"I think if I was probably a little bit more consistent, I would be better than I am.

"But talk is cheap and all that rubbish. I think I am good enough to beat anyone at the moment, because I like a scrap and no darts player wants to have a scrap.

"Most of them just want to have a little gallivant along the meadows and stuff like that, but I am quite happy to take them to a place where most of the younger players don't want to go and that is when I win games."

Luke Humphries, the 2023 Grand Slam champion, is also in action on Thursday night, against Tom Sykes, while Gian van Veen faces Martin Schindler and Nathan Aspinall takes on Gabriel Clemens.

Mardle: I don't get Van Gerwen at the moment

"There has been so much made of James Wade's form. He is playing great.

"I don't really get Michael van Gerwen at the moment. A couple of weeks ago he was playing in a Pro Tour event and was averaging 114, 115. He also looked great in his opening group game here, but then looked really edgy in his second.

"Having said that, normally with Michael, the longer the format the less edgy he looks. I'm not saying he'll beat James, but I don't buy into this narrative that Michael is off. He's just not as consistent as he used to be.

"He portrays a lack of confidence at times with what he says, which I don't like.

"I believe he is capable of growing into a game. His confidence grows after a couple of decent legs.

"But if James Wade gets on top of him, I don't like Van Gerwen's chances from there."

articles.title: Anthony Joshua drops major retirement hint before Tyson Fury fight, admits he has ‘not got many years’ left
articles.summary: Anthony Joshua is already thinking about life after boxing as he admits that his career could be nearing its end.
articles.body: Anthony Joshua is already thinking about life after boxing as he admits that his career could be nearing its end. The 37-year-old British heavyweight has revealed that he does not have many years left in the sport and expects retirement to come soon. Joshua is currently preparing for his long-awaited fight against Tyson Fury next month, but he is also considering what he wants to do once he leaves the ring. The boxer has even hinted at a possible business move, revealing that he could invest in sportswear giant Under Armour after retiring.Anthony Joshua admits retirement is getting closer after 13 years in professional boxingJoshua has been competing professionally for 13 years. Before turning professional, he won a gold medal at the London 2012 Olympics, which helped establish him as one of Britain’s biggest boxing names. Since then, he has become a two-time world heavyweight champion and built a professional record of 30 wins and four losses.However, the boxer now believes he is getting closer to the end of his career. Speaking in an exclusive interview with The Sun’s Clemmie Moodie, Joshua admitted that he is finding it difficult to believe he has already turned 37.“When am I going to retire? Pretty soon. I’m getting old now. From an athlete’s point of view, I’m getting old.“So maybe that will be our next sit down [interview], when we talk about plans for after boxing, because that will be coming around pretty soon. I haven’t got many years ahead of me.”His comments come ahead of his December 11 fight against Tyson Fury. The two British heavyweights are finally set to meet in a much-anticipated contest after years of talk about a possible showdown. Joshua has travelled to Marbella for his training camp as he prepares for the fight.Although his immediate attention remains on Fury, he has made it clear that he is also thinking about his future outside the ring.Anthony Joshua considers buying Under Armour shares after retirementJoshua has had a long business relationship with Under Armour, signing a sponsorship deal with the sportswear company in 2015. He renewed his contract in March 2024 and has also appeared in the brand’s international advertising campaigns.Now, the heavyweight has hinted that he could take that relationship further by becoming an investor after his boxing career ends. However, he made it clear that he is not looking to make any immediate changes to his business plans.“Boxing is not glamorous. I keep it pretty simple and straightforward.“I do what I can. I live by what I need, not by what I want. And it’s working out.“I think, when I finish fighting, I’ll be more chilled and then maybe I can go and look at investing in Under Armour stocks or maybe have a share in the Under Armour company. But as for now, I’m pretty content.”For now, Joshua’s focus is on his upcoming contest with Fury. articles.title: Chicago Cubs history unpacked — November 18
articles.summary: Happy Birthday, Jamie Moyer!
articles.body:
Free of charge for the discerning reader.

Happy birthday to Jamie Moyer, and a mighty host of others.

Today in baseball history, in 1987 – Chicago Cubs outfielder Andre Dawson becomes the first player from a last-place club ever to win an Most Valuable Player Award , taking National League honors with a .287 batting average and as the league leader in home runs (49) and RBI (137), and 2015 – In the Cy Young Award vote, Jake Arrieta of the Cubs is the winner in the Nationals League while Dallas Keuchel does the same in the American League . Both pitchers won their respective league's Wild Card Game with strong performances, in addition to being dominant in the regular season, and other stories as well.

1949 – Brooklyn Dodgers infielder Jackie Robinson , who hit 16 home runs with 124 RBI and led the National League with a .342 batting average, becomes the first African-American to win the Most Valuable Player Award .

1954 – The Kansas City Athletics hire Lou Boudreau as manager, replacing Eddie Joost , who is given his unconditional release . During his three-year tenure in Kansas City, the future Hall of Famer will pilot the second-division club to a 151-260 record.

1959 – Washington Senators outfielder Bob Allison is voted the American League Rookie of the Year . Allison led all major league rookies with 30 home runs and 85 RBI.

1964 – Baltimore Orioles third baseman Brooks Robinson is voted American League Most Valuable Player , outpolling Mickey Mantle of the New York Yankees 269 to 171.

1965 – Zoilo Versalles is named American League MVP . The Minnesota Twins shortstop gets 275 votes to 174 for teammate Tony Oliva .

1966 – Los Angeles Dodgers ace pitcher Sandy Koufax announces his retirement , due to increasing pain in his arthritic left elbow. Just three weeks earlier, Koufax won a record third Cy Young Award .

1980 – Despite having missed 45 games with injuries, George Brett is named American League Most Valuable Player . The 27-year-old third baseman's .390 batting average was the highest in the major leagues since Ted Williams hit .406 in 1941 . Brett added 24 home runs and 118 RBI to lead the Kansas City Royals to their first AL pennant .

1985 – Dwight Gooden of the New York Mets ( National League ) and Bret Saberhagen of the Kansas City Royals ( American League ) win the Cy Young Award in their respective leagues. St. Louis Cardinals outfielder Willie McGee , meanwhile, wins the National League Most Valuable Player Award , capping a season in which he led the league in batting average (.353) and hits (216) and also stole 56 bases.

1986 – Roger Clemens of the Boston Red Sox becomes the first starting pitcher to win the American League MVP Award since Vida Blue in 1971 , receiving 19 of a possible 28 first-place votes to defeat runner-up Don Mattingly .

1998 – For the second time in three seasons, Texas Rangers slugger Juan Gonzalez is voted the American League Most Valuable Player . A native of Puerto Rico , Gonzalez becomes the first Hispanic major leaguer to win two MVP awards.

1999 – Texas Rangers catcher Ivan Rodriguez wins the American League MVP Award . Rodriguez was runner-up for team MVP to Rafael Palmeiro .

2000 – The Seattle Mariners sign Japanese star outfielder Ichiro Suzuki to a three-year contract, making him the first Japanese position player in major league history.

2008 – Dustin Pedroia wins the 2008 American League Most Valuable Player Award . Pedroia led the American League in doubles and runs, nearly led in batting average and was among the leaders in total bases. He also stole 20 bases and won a Gold Glove in an all-around effort. Just last year, he was named Rookie of the Year . It had been 49 years since a second baseman – Nellie Fox – was named AL MVP.

2010 – Felix Hernandez of Seattle wins the 2010 American League Cy Young Award . In spite of a won-loss record of only 13-12 – the fewest wins by a starting pitcher to win the Cy Young Award in a full season -, "King Felix" draws voters' attention with his 2.27 ERA in 249.2 innings and 232 strikeouts.

2021 – Shohei Ohtani of the Angels is rewarded for his historic season as a two-way player by winning the 2021 American League Most Valuable Player Award . In the National League , it is Bryce Harper who is the winner, a second time for him as he also won the award in 2015 .

2024 – For the first time since 1981 , both winners of the Rookie of the Year Award are pitchers. In the National League , Paul Skenes prevails after going 11-3, 1.96 one year after being the first overall pick in the 2024 amateur draft . The vote is much closer in the American League where Luis Gil of the Yankees outpoints OF Colton Cowser of the Orioles

1914 – The Chicago Cubs name future Hall of Famer Roger Bresnahan as their manager . The former St. Louis Cardinals skipper will be in the dugout for just one year during which Chicago will finish fourth with a 73-80 record.

1951 – Former Chicago Cubs first baseman and future star of the TV series The Rifleman Chuck Connors becomes the first player to refuse to participate in the major league draft . Currently the 1B for the Los Angeles Angels of the Pacific Coast League , Connors wants to stay in California , instead of going to whatever team might draft him for the major leagues. The PCL views his refusal in a positive manner, allowing them to ask for higher prices for minor league players than what the major leagues usually offers.

1970 – Cincinnati Reds catcher Johnny Bench wins the National League MVP Award with 326 points, 108 more than Billy Williams of the Chicago Cubs . Bench hit for a .293 average with 45 home runs and 148 RBI, while Williams finished with .322, 42, 109.

1981 – Philadelphia Phillies third baseman Mike Schmidt wins his second consecutive National League MVP Award , joining Ernie Banks and Joe Morgan as the only NL players to take the award back-to-back. In the strike-shortened season, Schmidt hit .316 and led the league in home runs (31), RBI (91), runs (78), walks (73), on-base percentage (.435) and slugging percentage (.644).

1477 – "Dictes and Sayings of the Philosophers," the first dated printed book in England, is printed by William Caxton at his press in Westminster.

1865 – Mark Twain publishes the short story "The Celebrated Jumping Frog of Calaveras County" in The New York Saturday Press.

1872 – Suffragette Susan B. Anthony is arrested by a U.S. Deputy Marshal and charged with illegally voting.

1926 – George Bernard Shaw accepts the Nobel Prize for Literature but refuses the prize money, saying "I can forgive Alfred Nobel for inventing dynamite, but only a fiend in human form could have invented the Nobel Prize".

1970 – Future HOF boxer Joe Frazier KOs defending champion Bob Foster in second round at Cobo Arena, Detroit, for the WBA, WBC and The Ring heavyweight titles.

1978 – In Jonestown, Guyana, 918 members of the Peoples Temple are murdered or commit suicide under the leadership of cult leader Jim Jones .

1920 – Apollo Theater (Academy, Bryant) opens at 221 W. 42nd Street in NYC.

1993 – American rock band Nirvana films a mostly acoustic set at Sony Music Studios in New York City, for the television series MTV Unplugged.

1997 – Elektra Records (US) and Vertigo (worldide) release "Reload," the seventh studio album by American heavy metal band Metallica ; album tops the charts in 7 countries and garners worldwide sales of over 6 million units.

2002 – Mercury Nashville Records releases "Up!", the fourth studio album by Shania Twain (Billboard Album of the Year, 2003).

articles.body:
The Oklahoma Sooners will play their home finale for the 2026 season on Saturday, hosting the Texas A&M Aggies in Norman at 2:45 p.m. CT on ESPN2 . OU already celebrated Senior Day on September 19 in a Week 3 win against New Mexico, but a large group of Sooners will play their last game inside Gaylord Family-Oklahoma Memorial Stadium this week.

Oklahoma has two sixth-year players and 18 fifth-year players that will be out of collegiate eligibility after this season ends, and are therefore competing in their last home game on Saturday afternoon. That group of 20 players does not include players like defensive lineman David Stone or defensive back Peyton Bowen, both of whom seem likely to leave school early for the NFL draft. While not as likely to do so, players like defensive linemen Taylor Wein and Jayden Jackson also have stay-or-go-pro decisions to make after this season.

Of course, OU will lose a number of players to the transfer portal this offseason, just like every other team, but there are at least 20 Sooners who will close out their careers with Oklahoma and suit up for one final time on Owen Field this week.

articles.title: Kansas State Wildcats' Casey Alexander Keeping Team Grounded Despite Recent Success
articles.summary: The Kansas State Wildcats have won three straight since losing the season opener to South Dakota State
articles.body:
The Kansas State Wildcats have won three straight games since losing the season opener to the South Dakota State Jackrabbits.

The biggest reason for the change is because the Wildcats are starting to find a way to have a more balanced offensive attack. In Monday's win against the Montana Grizzlies, Kansas State had five players score in double figures in the 41-point victory.

This was especially important because the Wildcats were getting a little reliant on guard Brandon Rechsteiner. He had scored 26 points in the last two games to lead the team.

A strong balance should make the Wildcats a tougher team to defend the remainder of the non-conference schedule and especially when the Big 12 conference season begins.

Another issue first-year coach Casey Alexander is combating is overconfidence. He wants the Wildcats to remain grounded despite the recent success. They have one more game this Friday against the Campbell Fighting Camels before getting a huge test against the Gonzaga Bulldogs next week in Las Vegas. The Bulldogs are an annual contender for the NCAA Tournament, so it will give a good indicator of the progress Alexander has made with the program so far.

VICE HAVING SUCCESS AFTER TRANSFERRING FROM MURRAY STATE

Last Brock Vice was an afterthought when it came to scoring points on the basketball court.

Back then, he only averaged two points for the Murray State Racers. The lack of production led to a change of heart, so he decided to transfer to play for the Kansas State Wildcats.

Vice is coming off one of the best performances of his collegiate career. He finished with 10 points and 10 rebounds in Monday's victory against the Montana Grizzlies.

After the game, first-year Kansas State coach Casey Alexander even had to joke about it in his post-game press conference. Alexander said he didn't know if Vice had 10 points and 10 rebounds all of last season.

Actually, he did have season highs of 12 points and seven rebounds for the Racers but you get the point. This was a breakout performance for Vice. The coaching staff has been impressed with play this season. He's played with consistency while also being an effort and energy player. In his big game, Vice was 5 of 5 from the field in an efficient 16 minutes.

The hope is he can become a consistent inside presence for the Wildcats.

articles.title: Giants' Cam Skattebo says he's done doing backflip celebration after Aidan Hutchinson's injury
articles.summary: (AP) — New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo said he is done doing his signature backflip celebration after Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson...
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. (AP) — New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo said he is done doing his signature backflip celebration after Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson injured his right knee celebrating a sack Sunday against New England and is out for the rest of the season .

"It's hard to see," Skattebo told reporters from NJ.com and the New York Post after practice Wednesday. "Mentally, I'm like: 'I'm not doing that. That ain't going to happen to me.'"

Skattebo got into hot water with team officials over the summer when he landed awkwardly doing a backflip. He spent several months rehabbing from surgery to repair a broken right fibula and dislocated ankle.

"The big picture message is you want to take care of yourself," coach John Harbaugh said at the time. "You want to take care of your team. Do everything you can do to be healthy, be back, be right, be good."

Skattebo has rushed for 496 yards and four touchdowns on 116 carries in his second year in the NFL, including two scores last Thursday night against Washington. He lost a fumble in overtime in the first meeting against the Commanders on Oct. 11, which led him to getting only six offensive snaps and zero carries the following week when the Giants played New Orleans.

articles.title: Giants' Cam Skattebo has celebration update after Hutchinson injury
articles.summary: New York Giants running back and ex-Arizona State star Cam Skattebo said he's ending his backflip after touchdowns.
articles.body:
Cam Skattebo told the media on Wednesday, Nov. 18, that they won't be seeing his acrobatic backflips anymore.

The New York Giants star running back and former Arizona State standout, known for his backflip touchdown celebrations, saw the Detroit Lions' All-Pro pass rusher Aidan Hutchinson suffer a season-ending knee injury on Sunday, Nov. 15. Hutchinson joyfully leaped and his knee buckled upon landing after he sacked Drake Maye in their 35-10 home win against the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany.

Skattebo views that moment as a cautionary tale, especially after Skattebo's rookie season was cut short by a season-ending ankle injury during the Giants' Week 8 loss at Philadelphia in 2025.

"It's hard to see," Skattebo said about Hutchinson. "I'm saying yeah, no more backflips. Mentally, I'm like, 'I'm not doing that.' That ain't going to happen to me."

Skattebo, 24, said his backflip celly's potential return is contingent on "if we go to the playoffs or something," but will continue treading lightly because Hutchinson "didn't think about the risk either, and it happened."

Ex-ASU football star Cam Skattebo coming into Year 2 in the NFL

This will somewhat ease fans' fears for Skattebo regarding his physical style that's all power, no finesse in his carries. He caused a stir online July 18 when he did a high backflip and staggered afterward at Fanatics Fest in New York . Skattebo vowed to fans a day later at the event, "I will not hurt myself before the season."

Jesse Marsch shared his honest thoughts on the Canadian Premier League ahead of Cavalry vs. Atletico Ottawa this Saturday. The two clubs are set to meet in the CPL Final to determine the 2026 North Star Cup champion. Marsch complimented the league's quality and feels it continues to trend in the right direction.

The CPL launched in 2019 and serves as Canada's top-flight professional league. It has been a proving ground for many Canadian players who may not have previously received the same opportunities.

The CPL has continued to evolve, with 2026 being a historic season. Forge FC made history by defeating MLS-side CF Montreal to become the first CPL club to win the Canadian Championship.

"I think everybody sees the future as being bright in this country and [the] CPL continues to develop that. We've seen some new teams continue to emerge, some new coaches and players. I think that the playoffs have been spirited and fun to watch. articles.title: Baltimore Mayor rips Marlon Humphrey for letting down ‘young black boys’ with ‘criminals’ comment
articles.summary: In a recent episode of his podcast, Baltimore Ravens defensive back Marlon Humphrey answered “criminals” after being asked what Baltimore was best at making....
articles.body:
In a recent episode of his podcast, Baltimore Ravens defensive back Marlon Humphrey answered "criminals" after being asked what Baltimore was best at making.

"They're best at making criminals," Humphrey said on the show. "Yeah, no, that's obviously going to get cut out."

Unsurprisingly, Humphrey's comments led to widespread outrage, and he later issued an apology.

"I would like to apologize for some comments on my podcast I had yesterday, to the city of Baltimore," Humphrey told reporters, via the Associated Press. "I've been here my whole career, I've spent lots of offseasons here, welcomed a son here. I'm an investor in the city, investor in various parts of the state. Obviously, I do know the effect that words have, and just like to apologize for those comments."

Earnest as the apology may have been, Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott made it clear that an apology alone won't suffice.

"While we acknowledge Marlon's apology, a verbal apology is not enough. Baltimore is a city full of young Black boys who look to the Ravens as a beacon of light in their lives and to have someone that looks like them who wears a Baltimore Ravens jersey relegate them to becoming criminals cuts deeper," Scott said in a statement on social media. "I wonder how he would feel if prominent Baltimoreans used their platforms to imply that Baltimore once produced great defensive backs but we have recently lost our way.

"They wouldn't do that because our team and city are supposed to be united as one. Baltimore versus the world. I invite Marlon to sit down with me and some Baltimoreans who have re-entered into our community and are now preventing others from making the mistakes they made."

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter also addressed Humphrey's comments.

"Just speaking for myself, I love this city. I know what this city means to me and my family, and the opportunity that we've been granted here," he said. "Take a lot of pride in being here, and having been here before and choosing to come back here, it's a great city with a bunch of great people. We desperately want to represent this city the right way by how we play."

The Ravens are 4-6, and patience with the franchise is running thin among Ravens fans, and Humphrey is insisting that he remains committed to giving those fans the experience they deserve, despite his comments and the way the season has gone.

"I love the city," he said. "I think I've expressed this many times: I want to win in front of the fans, just because it's not cheap to be in those seats."

articles.title: Eddie Robinson Jr knows winning is only part of Alabama State's retention battle
articles.summary: Eddie Robinson Jr. knows winning now matters, but Alabama State also has to convince its players that Montgomery is where they belong in the future.
articles.body:
The chances for Alabama State football to reach the SWAC title game are all but gone. The Hornets could be considered in a three-way tie if Alabama A&M loses and Jackson State wins, but Alabama State would be the first team eliminated in that scenario.

That isn't stopping the Hornets from what's in front of them this weekend with reigning SWAC champion Prairie View A&M coming to Montgomery on Saturday, Nov. 21. But coach Eddie Robinson Jr. knows he has to think about what's to come next season.

The transfer portal creates opportunity for players to move elsewhere, and Alabama State knows it has to make sure its current roster wants to stay in Montgomery.

During his weekly press conference on Wednesday, Nov. 18, Robinson recalled a lesson he learned last season.

Alabama State's players were receiving interest from other programs as early as the third game on 2025's schedule. This year, the Alabama State coaching staff started having conversations with players about returning next season much earlier, beginning around the second week of the season.

"Those guys that we feel like you want to have come back the next year, you have to start those conversations early," Robinson said. "And they've got to be continual because, you know, other people are talking to them as well."

Photographs of the Alabama State vs. Jackson State football game

Robinson said retaining players requires a proactive approach, particularly as programs compete for the same talent. He pointed to the overall student-athlete experience, the atmosphere surrounding wins and the financial opportunities available to players as factors in those decisions.

Alabama State's 20-13 home victory against Jackson State last week provided an example of the environment Robinson wants players to experience.

He highlighted the crowd, the involvement of students and the interaction between players and fans following the game, saying those moments create memories that can make players want to return.

"It's our job just to kind of put them in an environment so they can have those memories to make them want to come back," Robinson said.

The Hornets also have young contributors they hope to build around. Robinson pointed to the number of young players seeing significant action on defense, saying the program expects several of them to return.

For Alabama State, finishing the season strong is about more than adding another victory. It's also an opportunity to continue building an environment and a roster the program hopes will carry into next season.

articles.title: Nets look to overcome losing woes vs. Nic Claxton, Bulls on ABA Night
articles.summary: The Brooklyn Nets have not played as well as they wanted to thus far in the season, but Wednesday's matchup against the Chicago Bulls could fix that.
articles.body:
NEW YORK -- The Brooklyn Nets (3-10) have not yet "shocked the world" like they set out to do when training camp began in September following an exciting offseason of moves. Brooklyn has not been able to be on the same page as a young team that has several new players in the rotation, but the Nets are hoping to draw some inspiration from players in previous generations.

"I think that winning can be absorbed by the kids. I think that would be the best thing, and a lot of that comes with the work, but also building that connected team," Fernandez said to the media prior to Wednesday's matchup against the Chicago Bulls . Not only will former Nets center Nic Claxton be making his return to Barclays Center for the first time since he was traded this offseason, but "ABA Night" should give the players some extra juice as well.

"I see it the other way. It's 'this is what we did to get back into the game,' right? Instead of bringing too many negatives into [it], it's this is the type of team we want to be with cleaner coverages, but also being the aggressor," Fernandez explained when asked how the team can prevent falling behind by double digits. "At this moment, I want to focus on the positives and how to clean up and teach some of the things that we didn't do as well in the first half."

The Nets enter Wednesday's matchup against the Bulls on a two-game losing streak and in their losses to the Memphis Grizzlies and Philadelphia 76ers, Brooklyn trailed by as many as 26 points and 24 points, respectively. Conversely, in the Nets' three wins this season, they have only trailed by 10 points or fewer in those matchups so the message is clear that Brooklyn has to find a way to prevent their bad stretches from snowballing.

"Punch first. [It's as] simple as that. Punch first. If we punch first, and be aggressive, good things happen," Nets forward Julius Randle said to the media prior to the matchup against Chicago. Brooklyn has had some issues with punching first, especially against the better teams in the NBA, but the hope is that the allure of ABA Night and the lessons learned from previous losses can help this young group get off to a good start at home.

That's Adam Gaudette on the top line, Macklin Celebrini and Will Smith split up, Barclay Goodrow on the second line, Michael Misa and Tyler Toffoli on the fourth line, along with Collin Graf and Michael Kesselring potentially sitting out.

Don't count on these being the lines on Saturday, though a couple changes could stick.

"Just get a look at some guys in different spots. We've kept our top-six [together], for the most part, give some guys other opportunities and see what they look like," San Jose Sharks head coach Ryan Warsofsky said. "We got a couple days here. We don't play till Saturday, so we have some time."

Warsofsky didn't share the purpose of these lines today, if they don't plan on using them.

There was a clear message to the team though.

The San Jose Sharks practiced for over an hour…then ended with a bag skate.

"Just a wake-up call," Ty Dellandrea said. "We didn't really meet about it, but that was the unwritten message. I think it's just we got to play harder and got to compete."

"We're gonna have practices like this," Dellandrea said.

"As a coach," Warsofsky said, "you got to find different ways, sometimes, to get your message across."

"[Defensive] arrivals," Warsofsky said. "Breaking out of pucks as [a group of] five, being connected. Working up and down the ice."

"A lot of D-zone, a lot of battle," Dellandrea said. "Coming into our D-zone connected, coming back hard, tracking back hard. And then, being quick to close on people who are circling around the corner."

So the plan seems clear…but can the San Jose Sharks execute it?

They don't practice on Thursday, are back at it on Friday, then take on the Seattle Kraken on Saturday.

articles.title: Lakers Get Mixed Austin Reaves, Luka Doncic News Before Jazz Game
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers receive mixed injury news on Austin Reaves, Luka Doncic and Walker Kessler before facing Utah. The post Lakers Get Mixed Austin Reaves...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Lakers will have Luka Dončić available for the second night of a back-to-back, but their winning streak will face another test without Austin Reaves.

Reaves has been ruled out of Wednesday's game against the Utah Jazz because of a left heel contusion and bone bruise, according to the Lakers injury report.

The encouraging news is that Dončić will play, while starting center Walker Kessler returns after missing Tuesday's overtime victory over Charlotte.

The updates come less than 24 hours after the Lakers rallied from an 18-point deficit to defeat the Hornets 118-114, extending their winning streak to nine games.

Austin Reaves Ruled Out Again Against Utah Jazz

Reaves will miss his third consecutive game as he continues recovering from the heel injury.

The absence is significant for a Lakers team that has relied heavily on his production alongside Dončić.

Reaves is averaging 24.7 points this season, providing Los Angeles with another reliable scorer and playmaker.

Without him, coach JJ Redick has leaned more heavily on Quentin Grimes.

That adjustment paid off spectacularly Tuesday.

Grimes erupted for a career-high 47 points against Charlotte, making 10 three-pointers to join Kobe Bryant as the only Lakers players to reach that milestone.

His final three-pointer tied the game with 1.7 seconds remaining in regulation.

The Lakers eventually completed the comeback in overtime.

Grimes' emergence has helped Los Angeles overcome Reaves' absence, although his continued production will be important against Utah.

Luka Doncic Cleared to Play on Back-to-Back

Dončić's availability provides another significant lift.

The NBA's leading scorer played heavy minutes Tuesday, finishing with 36 points as Los Angeles improved to 13-2.

Despite the short turnaround, the Lakers will have their primary offensive creator available against the Jazz.

Dončić is averaging 39 points this season and has been central to Los Angeles' impressive start.

He also has a recent history of success against Utah.

In their previous meeting, Dončić scored 52 points, helping the Lakers escape with a narrow victory.

His presence becomes especially important with Reaves unavailable.

The Lakers will need Dončić to continue creating scoring opportunities while Grimes and the supporting cast provide additional offense.

Walker Kessler Returns Against Former Team

Kessler's return offers Los Angeles help in another area.

The center missed Tuesday's game because of right lower leg soreness, ending his streak of appearances to begin the season.

His absence forced the Lakers to adjust their frontcourt rotation against Charlotte.

Now, Kessler is set to face the Jazz, the franchise where he began his NBA career.

The matchup offers an intriguing reunion for the former Utah center.

His rebounding, rim protection and interior presence should help Los Angeles manage its frontcourt minutes following Tuesday's overtime game.

The Lakers enter Wednesday riding their longest winning streak of the season.

With little recovery time and Reaves still sidelined, Los Angeles must rely on Dončić, Kessler and its suddenly productive supporting cast to keep the streak alive.
